packageRules.description: Security-first posture: suppress all routine (non-security) version updates. vulnerabilityAlerts force-overrides this for vulnerable deps, so security PRs still open.
Re-enable end-of-life / end-of-support PRs (endoflife-date datasource). Auto-detected, no annotation needed; tolerant of false positives.

Node runtime, every place it is pinned, in ONE grouped PR. The .nvmrc manager below uses endoflife-date and so is already re-enabled, but the native managers extract the same runtime under the node-version datasource (package.json engines/volta, .node-version) and the docker datasource (Dockerfile FROM node) — datasources the catch-all disable above swallows. That is why nodejs v24 moved .nvmrc alone and left engines.node warning EBADENGINE with the container image still building on 22 (classroomready_backend#300 -> #413). No matchUpdateTypes filter: repos pin majors, so minors have nothing to rewrite, and a filter here would drop a range-style engines value (cms uses >=22.0.0) out of the group and reintroduce the drift. LTS-only tags and the -alpine suffix are already handled by workarounds:nodeDockerVersioning, inherited via config:recommended; the calico/kindest negations mirror that preset because the node regex is broad.

@types/node rides in the same group as the runtime — the type surface has to match the engine it compiles against, and a lagging major is the third half of the drift described above. workarounds:typesNodeVersioning (also via config:recommended) already gives this package node versioning, so it follows runtime majors. NOTE: this rule must NOT carry matchUpdateTypes. updateType is only known after the version lookup, and the catch-all rule above disables this dep before that lookup happens, so a rule combining matchUpdateTypes with enabled:true never fires — verified by dry-run, @types/node stayed skipReason:disabled. Majors-only is enforced by the next rule instead, which filters updates after lookup.

Keep ordinary DefinitelyTyped churn out: only a @types/node MAJOR (i.e. a runtime major) is wanted, so drop the rest now that the dep itself is enabled. Filtering updates after lookup works in this direction, unlike re-enabling.

customManagers.description: Terraform CLI pin (hashicorp/setup-terraform terraform_version input) -> endoflife-date

RDS/Aurora Postgres engine_version -> endoflife-date. Recursive: the outer regex isolates the `rds_master = { ... }` block (bounded by its own closing brace), the inner regex finds engine_version within just that block, so only that line is ever rewritten and a sibling Redis engine_version can't be matched.

ElastiCache Redis engine_version -> endoflife-date. Recursive, same as the Postgres manager above but scoped to a `redis = { ... }` block; depName is amazon-elasticache-redis (verified on endoflife.date), NOT the community `redis` slug, since ElastiCache's supported versions (currently 7.x) lag community Redis (already 8.x).
